correctness.rationale: A selected spine vertex observes the other spine vertex and one internal vertex on every page, after which each page forces completely. Without a selected spine vertex, each touched page is fully observed in the domination step. At most one untouched page can then be entered by forcing from the spine, whereas two untouched pages leave at least two unobserved neighbors at each spine endpoint and permanently block propagation. The three resulting disjoint set classes yield the polynomial exactly. Exhaustive subset checks for r=2..8 confirm the structural criterion, all coefficients, totals, and minimum counts.

value.rationale: Book graphs are a standard named family explicitly used in later domination-counting work. The theorem completely classifies every power dominating set, gives the full polynomial and total count, and identifies the minimum PMU placements. It therefore advances the counting objective of the foundational polynomial paper and fills a natural family omission highlighted by later literature.
